Admissions
Admissions
If you have a question about a course or need permissions into the course, please email chemistry@unlv.edu. Permissions will only be granted this way, not over the phone. Please allow 24 hours for a response.
Undergraduate Admissions
Minimum GPA
2.50
Admission Policies
Students must meet minimum GPA requirements. Probationary admission may be provided for those students with a GPA between 2.30 and 2.49. See the department for further details.
Transfer Policies
Transfer students first should have their transcripts evaluated by student enrollment services, then schedule a meeting with the College of Sciences Advising Center. Based on the transcripts and catalog descriptions, equivalencies to UNLV courses will be determined and a plan for completion of the degree will be developed. In cases of questions regarding the transferability of a particular course, satisfactory performance (i.e., a grade of C or better) by a student in a higher numbered UNLV chemistry course for which the proposed UNLV transfer course is a prerequisite shall be accepted as proof that the student has mastery of the course content and the student shall be awarded transfer credit.
The undergraduate application is online. Simply follow the steps on the university's admissions page. You'll find information for freshmen, transfer students, and international students.
When filling out the undergraduate application, be sure to indicate your major in the College of Sciences.
Graduate Admissions
Admission to the master's program requires an undergraduate degree in chemistry, biochemistry, biology, or a related discipline, with a cumulative GPA of 2.75 or of 3.00 for the last two years of undergraduate work. Applicants seeking a Ph.D. must have a minimum grade point average of 3.00 on a 4.0 scale, and must have a B.S. degree or an M.S. degree in biochemistry, chemistry, or a related discipline.
Important Note: Graduate applications for students interested in the radiochemistry program should be directed to professor Art Gelis, radiochemistry program director.
Dec 1: Standard Admissions Deadline
Applications for fall admission must be completed by Dec 1. The Department does not admit students for the spring semester.
Degree Requirements
A minimum of 30 graduate credits is required for the M.S., 60 for the Ph.D. A GPA of at least 3.00 must be achieved in all course work required for the degree. No grade lower than C is acceptable, and only one grade below B- is permitted.
Research and course work specializations are available in analytical chemistry, biochemistry, chemistry education, organic chemistry, and physical chemistry. The individual student's program of course work must be selected in consultation with and approved by the student's committee, and may include courses from selected disciplines other than chemistry, such as biology, physics, civil and environmental engineering, or water resources management.
Students are expected to select a research advisor by the end of their first semester.
Each student is required to present a departmental seminar on the student's research prior to graduation. This requirement is in addition to the CHEM 791 credits required for the degree programs. Students are expected to attend weekly departmental seminars.
Each student is required to meet at least once per semester with the student's examination committee. At the meeting in the semester prior to the expected term of graduation, the student will be asked to make a detailed presentation on research progress. The committee then will make recommendations to be addressed by the student during the remainder of the student's research program, in writing the thesis/dissertation, and in the final examination. The committee may request another meeting prior to the final exam if deemed necessary.
It is expected that each student will be a teaching assistant for a minimum of two courses prior to graduation. It also is expected that each student publish at least one research-based manuscript in a peer-reviewed journal.
Application
Chemistry/biochemistry master’s and chemistry Ph.D. students must apply for admission through the graduate admission application page. Applicants should submit materials to meet both the UNLV Graduate College and the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry requirements.

Statement of Interest (one-to-two pages)
The Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry evaluates applicants using a holistic review, which is an evidence-based approach to identify people who are likely to be successful in chemistry and biochemistry research, regardless of opportunities that may or may not have been available to them. Applicants are encouraged to specifically address the following criteria in their statements of interest. It may also be useful for letter writers to address criteria about which they have direct knowledge.
Research potential. The applicant’s capacity to conduct significant, original scientific investigation that advances the field; the applicant’s capacity to succeed in rigorous doctoral research
Academic readiness and growth trajectory. The applicant’s prerequisite knowledge, skills, and cognitive abilities that will allow them to succeed in graduate-level chemistry courses
Communication and critical thinking. The applicant’s ability to (1) clearly and persuasively articulate ideas and thought processes in written and oral formats and (2) understand, analyze, synthesize, and evaluate scientific information to form logical conclusions and solve complex problems
Interpersonal skills and collegiality. The applicant’s capacity to work effectively and respectfully with peers, advisors, and others in the scientific community
Motivation and long-term goals. The applicant’s motivation for pursuing a graduate degree in chemistry, including factors such as scientific curiosity, a passion for the field, a desire to improve personal knowledge and skills, chemistry-related future career plans, and a desire to make meaningful contributions to the field and/or to society
Leadership potential. The applicant’s capacity to mentor others, take initiative to support peers, advocate for positive changes, and/or ensure research safety
